You have foundational Excel and presentation skills from class projects, and an interest in operations, finance, and analytics. Your target roles typically require junior-level coursework and hands-on experience that you're still building.

must_have_gaps.why_it_matters: National occupational survey data rates this knowledge area at 84 out of 100 for Management Analysts (your Business Analyst Intern target)—it is considered essential for the role.

must_have_gaps.how_to_close: Seek a part-time customer-facing role or volunteer position that involves client interaction, or take a course in services marketing (e.g., MKTG 321).

must_have_gaps.how_to_close: Continue with your accounting sequence (ACCT 230 next) and add a microeconomics course (ECON 202) to deepen your understanding of economic principles.
must_have_gaps.why_it_matters: Personal Financial Advisors, the closest occupation national survey data covers for your Finance Intern target, rate this at 77 out of 100. It is a must-have for that role.

nice_to_have_gaps.why_it_helps: Rated 66 out of 100 for Management Analysts and 68 for Personal Financial Advisors—having stronger quantitative reasoning can differentiate you.

nice_to_have_gaps.how_to_close: After the Google Data Analytics Certificate, practice building dashboards in Tableau Public using the same project dataset.
nice_to_have_gaps.why_it_helps: Both tools appear in hot technology lists for Business Analyst and Finance Intern roles—they make your data work visible and compelling.

data.role_evolution_summary: Across your three target internship roles, the biggest shift is from doing manual data entry, drafting, and research to curating and validating AI-generated work. Interns are now expected to use business judgment to interpret outputs, spot errors, and focus on stakeholder communication and process improvement. AI is becoming a tool you work alongside, not a replacement for your role.
